title: Car Fleet
pattern: Sort by position, compare arrival times
statement: Cars drive along a one-lane road toward `target`. Car `i` starts at `position[i]` with `speed[i]`. A car cannot overtake: when it catches a slower car it slows down and they continue together as one **fleet**. Return how many fleets arrive at the target.

example.why: The cars at 10 and 8 arrive together, the cars at 5 and 3 merge, and the car at 0 arrives alone.

idea: A car can only be held up by cars **ahead** of it. So handle the cars from the one nearest the target back to the farthest.
For each car compute the time it would need to reach the target *if the road were empty*: `(target − position) / speed`.
If that time is not longer than the fleet in front needs, the car catches up and joins it. If it is longer, it never catches up — it leads a new fleet.

complexity.timeWhy: Sorting the cars dominates; the scan afterwards is O(n).

steps.text: Our example: **`target = 12, position = [10,8,0,5,3], speed = [2,4,1,1,3]`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
